title: EV Charger (EVSE) Output Check
description: Verify Level 2 EVSE output voltage and delivered current are within expected limits during a charging session.

steps.title: Safety And Setup
steps.instruction: SAFETY: EVSE circuits are 208-240 V and high current. Confirm PPE and CAT rating. Only access live terminals if qualified; prefer measuring at the equipment disconnect. Never clamp or probe inside the connector handle.
steps.note_prompt: Record EVSE model, rated output amps, and supply breaker size.

steps.title: Measure Output Voltage
steps.instruction: With the EVSE energized, set the meter to AC voltage and measure line-to-line output voltage at the supply terminals. Capture the reading. A 240 V nominal supply should sit roughly between 208 V and 264 V.

acceptance.description: 208-240 V nominal EVSE supply, allowing +10% high limit.

steps.title: Measure Charging Current
steps.instruction: Start a charging session and let it ramp to steady state. Clamp one supply conductor and capture the delivered AC current. It should not exceed the EVSE rated output current.

acceptance.description: Typical Level 2 EVSE output up to 48 A continuous; set max to the EVSE rating.

steps.note_prompt: Record steady-state charging current vs the EVSE rating.

steps.title: Record Result
steps.instruction: Document the session. Low or unstable voltage under load, or current well below rating, may indicate supply or EVSE derating issues.
